fixes.explanation: I see why that sounds nice, friend. But the LORD says the opposite: "…very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) Joshua, Israel's leader, is old and well along in years, and there's still plenty left to take. It's like pulling a tray out of the oven and finding three more batches of dough waiting.

Reuben and Gad are a fair guess, since they do come up in this chapter. But they had already received their inheritance from Moses beyond the Jordan (Joshua 13:8). This land is for "…the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) Their batch was already baked, boxed and sealed.

False is right, baker! The text says, "…the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day." (Joshua 13:13) Just before that, Moses, Israel's leader, had struck down Og's kingdom and dispossessed them (Joshua 13:12). So this verse is the one spot where the cleanup didn't get finished. It's like sweeping the counter and finding a few crumbs still sitting right there.

Yes, baker! Levi is the tribe set apart to serve the LORD, and Moses gave them no land. Their inheritance is this: "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) A few verses later it's said again: "The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:33) Every other tribe got a map with borders, and Levi got a promise instead. I think that's worth a second look.
